facts.material: Laminated film: polyethylene terephthalate (PET) laminated to polyethylene (two plastic layers); exact weight share not provided
facts.function: Flexible packaging film for packaging products
facts.form: Non-cellular, laminated plastic film/roll or sheet, finished (not described as part or set)
facts.end_use: Used by packagers/manufacturers to wrap or package products

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 3920 covers other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials; heading 3920.62 covers films 'Of poly(ethylene terephthalate)'
Check Chapter 39 notes (polymers and composites): Note 4 — polymer blends/composites are classified by the polymer which predominates by weight; laminated/supported films fall in heading 3920
GRI 3(b): For composite goods of different materials, classify according to the material giving the essential character (here the predominant polymer by weight/value/role).

rejected_alternatives.reason: This heading is for films 'Of polymers of ethylene' (polyethylene). It would apply only if the polyethylene layer predominates by weight/value/essential character; available facts indicate PET component is a primary material so 3920.62 is preferred.
Chapter 39 headings for primary forms of plastics/materials (e.g., waste or primary forms) do not describe finished laminated film articles; 3920 specifically covers laminated films.

missing_facts: Relative proportion by weight (or by surface area/thickness) of PET vs. polyethylene in the laminate — determines which polymer predominates and thus the correct 6-digit heading if polyethylene predominates
Thicknesses or any special coatings/metalization (if present) that could affect subheading selection
classification.rationale: The product is a noncellular laminated plastic film used for packaging and falls under chapter 39 heading 3920 (films, laminated). When a film consists of PET laminated to polyethylene, classification is by the polymer that gives the essential character (chapter 39 note re: polymer predominance). If PET predominates, heading 3920.62 ('Of poly(ethylene terephthalate)') applies. Recent CBP rulings on PET films (e.g., N326371, N338010) classify similar PET laminated/coated films under 3920.62. Given the description (PET laminated to polyethylene) and absent a statement that polyethylene predominates, the most likely 10-digit statistical line is 3920.62.00.50 (Other).

facts.function: Floor covering (tiles) for installation as flooring
facts.form: Tiles (finished floor tiles), not otherwise described (no layer/core detail provided)
facts.end_use: Used by consumers/professional installers as floor covering

gri_path: GRI 1: Chapter 39 headings (3918) cover "Floor coverings of plastics ... in the form of tiles; of polymers of vinyl chloride: vinyl tile"
GRI 6: Choose statistical subheading within 3918.10.10 (rigid solid polymer core; rigid expanded polymer core; other)

rejected_alternatives.reason: Chapter 42 covers leather and certain articles of leather — not applicable to plastic (PVC) floor tiles.
This subheading is specific to vinyl tile consisting of a rigid expanded polymer core; no information provided that the tile has an expanded core.
This "Other" statistical line applies when the tile does not meet the definitions of the rigid solid or rigid expanded polymer core lines; classification depends on core construction.

missing_facts: Is the tile homogenous/mass vinyl (solid PVC) or does it have a rigid solid polymer core (stone plastic composite/SPC) or a rigid expanded core (foam/expanded polymer)?
If a layered product, what are the layer materials and thicknesses (wear layer, core composition and thickness)?
classification.rationale: PVC floor tiles fall in chapter 39 heading 3918 (floor coverings of plastics: of polymers of vinyl chloride: vinyl tile). The HTS provides statistical subheadings distinguishing rigid solid polymer core, rigid expanded polymer core, and other vinyl tile; the product description lacks core/layer detail needed to select the precise 10-digit line. Based on common PVC tiles, 3918.10.10.20 (vinyl tile consisting of a rigid solid polymer core) is the likeliest line, but confirmation of core construction is required to be certain.

facts.form: made-up, finely knit jersey fabric, rib knit crew neckline, short hemmed sleeves, straight hemmed bottom; boys' T-shirt
facts.end_use: worn by boys as everyday apparel

gri_path: GRI 1: Chapter 61 (knitted garments) applies; heading 6109 covers T-shirts, singlets, tank tops and similar garments, knitted or crocheted
GRI 1: Read heading text and subheadings under 6109 to find 'Of cotton' (6109.10) and 'Of other textile materials' (6109.90) and the 'of man-made fibers' subdivision (6109.90.10)

GRI 3(b): Goods consisting of a mixture of cotton and man-made fiber qualify under the component which gives them their essential character; practice and rulings apply an 85% cotton threshold for classification 'of cotton' in Chapter 61, so a 50/50 blend does not fall in 'of cotton'
GRI 6: Selected the boys' statistical line under 6109.90.10 (6109.90.10.25) as the appropriate 10-digit HTSUS leaf
classification.deciding_gri: GRI 1, applied with GRI 3(b) (mixture rule / chapter practice on cotton content)

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 'of cotton' (6109.10) would apply only when garment contains predominantly cotton (practice uses ~85%+ cotton); the product is 50% cotton/50% polyester so excluded.
Statistical line for 'T-shirts, all white' — not applicable (product not specified as all white and also composition excludes 'of cotton' line).

missing_facts: none essential for 6-digit heading; if you require absolute certainty on the statistical suffix, provide the garment's exact HTS statistical category or any distinguishing features (e.g., printed/embroidered trim, or whether considered 'thermal' underwear) — otherwise 6109.90.10.25 (boys') is the applicable current leaf
classification.rationale: The goods are made-up knitted T-shirts (Chapter 61, heading 6109). Because the fabric is a 50/50 cotton/polyester blend it does not meet the customary threshold for classification 'of cotton' (6109.10), so it falls under 'Of other textile materials — Of man-made fibers' (6109.90.10) and the boys' statistical line. CROSS ruling I89898 (in force) on mixed cotton/poly garments supports treating blends that are not predominantly cotton as outside the 'of cotton' subheading.
